conviction_note: No consensus exists, so the bar is the prior-year Q2 ($4.62m revenue, -$0.15 EPS) and management's stated 'plan' for year-over-year improvement in Q2. The only company-level leading number, active Brand Partners held at about 5,200 to July 9 against a 5,800 average in last year's Q2 and in a quarter management calls seasonally one of its lowest, points to a revenue decline of roughly 5-15% and a missed plan. Lower G&A and no interest expense should narrow the pre-tax loss, but with no tax benefit (valuation allowance) EPS likely lands near last year's -$0.15. Findings sum to -0.7. Scaled: abs 3.5 (median reaction 3.18, nudged up because Q2 is the seasonal trough and the stock trades about $26k a day) times p_up 42 (6 of 7 prior prints fell, lean from partner count) = -0.56. The two measurements agree in sign and size.
bar: No sell-side consensus found for the August-2026 quarter (FXEmpire estimate fields blank, TipRanks one analyst on a different quarter: https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/educ/earnings). Bar used is the prior-year Q2 FY2026: revenue $4,621,100, pre-tax loss $(1,750,200), net loss $(1,294,700), EPS $(0.15), avg Brand Partners 5,800 (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/269893/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2026-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Results), plus management's own Q2 'plan' of year-over-year improvement stated on the July 9 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15219109458093056). Unsourced as a consensus, so every size is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest about 11.9k shares at the 2026-06-30 FINRA settlement, days to cover about 1.0, borrow fee 5.9% (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/educ/, page updated 2026-07-14); Equibles shows 5,892 shares short at 2026-03-13 settlement with days to cover 1.00 (https://equibles.com/stocks/educ/shortinterest). Well under 1% of 8.51m shares, so no crowded short and no squeeze mechanism. No option market (baseline status no_options_market), so no skew. Baseline: spot $1.315, run-up +1.15% over 5 and 20 days, 20.3% below 52-week high and 6.05% above the low, realised vol 6.2% annualised, average volume 19.6k shares (about $26k a day). No Form 4 filings since 2025-11-18 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000031667&type=4&dateb=&owner=include&count=20).

findings.finding: The revenue driver is flat-to-down into Q2: management said on the July 9 call that active Brand Partners were 'above 5,200' after the March Pi Day promotion and had 'maintained this level ... to this day', while Q2 FY2026 averaged 5,800 partners on $4.62m of revenue; at roughly the same revenue per partner a ~5,200 base implies Q2 FY2027 revenue near $4.0-4.4m, i.e. a 5-15% decline against the prior year and against management's stated plan of year-over-year improvement ('I'm not saying it is, but that's the plan'), in a quarter they describe as 'one of the lowest quarters for us as a whole'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue and partner count are the headline lines of every release. Q1 FY2027 (revenue -33% YoY, partners 5,300 vs 7,700) fell -3.18%; Q2 FY2026 (revenue -29%, partners 5,800 vs 13,900) fell -9.94%; 6 of the last 7 prints fell, median absolute 3.18% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: There is no consensus and no analyst model, so nobody has translated the partner count into a Q2 revenue number; if the market had priced a stabilisation narrative the stock would not be sitting 6% above its 52-week low with zero run-up. The flip side: the YoY decline narrowing from -33% to roughly -10% could read as stabilisation, which is why the range spans positive.
findings.independence: The partner and revenue history comes from the company's own releases: Q1 FY2027 release (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/304633/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2027-First-Quarter-Results) gives avg 5,300 and 5,200 at end-May; Q2 FY2026 release (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/269893/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2026-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Results) gives 5,800 and $4.62m. No independent third-party series on PaperPie activity was found.

findings.finding: The cost base and interest line are lower than last year's Q2: G&A cuts expected to save over $1.2m in FY2027 (about $0.3m a quarter), Q1 operating expenses fell to $4.10m from $5.70m, bank debt was repaid from the Nov-2025 Hilti Complex sale (Q1 interest expense $600), so the Q2 pre-tax loss should narrow from $(1.75)m even on lower revenue; but no tax benefit is recorded now (valuation allowance), so EPS likely lands near last year's $(0.15).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY2027 showed the same pattern (pre-tax loss $(1.38)m vs $(1.45)m, but net loss wider on the tax line) and the stock fell -3.18%; the market has not rewarded narrower pre-tax losses on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: No estimate exists to embed it; the headline EPS comparison will look flat-to-worse because of the absent tax benefit, so the improvement is only visible to someone reading the pre-tax line.
findings.independence: Q1 FY2027 release states the $1.2m G&A saving plan (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/304633/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2027-First-Quarter-Results); same company, partly the same document family.

findings.finding: The Usborne distribution agreement is terminable at Usborne's option: the May-quarter 10-Q says EDC missed minimum purchase volumes in FY2025 and FY2026, did not meet letter-of-credit requirements, and that 'certain payments were not received timely'; Usborne purchases were $0 in the quarter and Usborne titles fell to 33.1% of PaperPie revenue from 44.4%, with $19.6m of Usborne inventory on the balance sheet. No termination notice had been received.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The compliance language has sat in the 10-K and 10-Qs for over a year without a notice; no print has turned on it.
findings.why_not_priced: It is disclosed, so the risk is partly priced; what is not priced is any change in status, which would appear only in the Q2 10-Q or call. Most likely the language repeats unchanged (hence the small size); a notice would be a large negative (low end).
findings.independence: FY2026 10-K carries the same minimum-purchase language (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000031667/000118518526001927/educ10k022826.htm); same company documents.

findings.finding: Liquidity rests on liquidating inventory in the seasonal trough: cash $1.66m (plus $0.15m restricted) at May 31, Q1 operating cash flow +$0.56m came from a $1.42m inventory reduction, the only facility is a $2.0m Regent Bank revolver at prime+2% maturing 2027-03-06 and personally guaranteed by the CEO; the 10-Q has no going-concern language and management aims to be 'cash flow positive'. Asked what the money buys: it funds operating losses, not a demand ramp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY2027 cash rose to $1.8m and the stock still fell -3.18%; no print has been read on the cash line alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Market cap is about $11m (8.51m shares x $1.315) against $41.4m of book equity and $36.2m of inventory, so the market already discounts the inventory heavily; a summer cash draw toward the revolver or a revolver draw would sharpen the funding question before the March 2027 maturity. If cash rose again, this reverses (high end).
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as findings 2 and 3; CFO cash commentary on the call (https://www.webull.com/news/15219109458093056).

outside_window.finding: Regent Bank $2.0m revolver matures 2027-03-06; a renewal or non-renewal is the next financing event.

rejected_candidates.detail: A 2025 event resolved by the Nov-2025 building sale and the March-2026 Regent Bank facility; it has no bearing on this print.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Assets held for sale write-downs on the legacy pick-and-pack system ($113.6k in Q1, $450k carrying value left)
rejected_candidates.detail: Immaterial below-the-line item at most $0.45m; folded into the cost/loss finding (finding 2) rather than filed separately.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Disputed, unrecognised $1.0m FY2022 Usborne volume rebate
rejected_candidates.detail: Part of the Usborne relationship finding (finding 3); a resolution either way would be a one-off.

baseline_tension: No skew or option market exists; the small negative lean agrees with the name's own reaction history (6 of 7 prints down) and with a stock pinned 6% above its 52-week low with no run-up, so it is consistent with, not against, what is priced, and the illiquidity ($26k a day) means the realised move is noisy.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar unsourced: no consensus, only prior-year and a management 'plan'): kept every finding capped small; trimmed the partner-count finding from -0.8 to -0.7.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the revolver and inventory liquidation fund losses rather than a ramp, but there is no going-concern language and cash rose last quarter, so the liquidity finding moved from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 2/3 (one-off and own caveat): the Usborne termination right is long-disclosed with no notice received, so its expected value moved from -0.3 to -0.2 with the tail kept in the low end.
Lesson 1 and 7 (reaction function, positioning): no change to abs_move_pct 3.5 or p_up 42; short interest checked and not crowded.
